content.html:
• New week, new me, and all that. Some new routines are settling, and the combination of not making plans and a few people returning from leave has left me with time, for the first time in a while. Time I have already accounted for.
  • Firstly, I received an actual letter in the mail, about how to write a letter. I kind-of want to frame it. And now I feel inspired to buy a typewriter of my own.
  • Weather was so perfect and delightful for the week, right up until the weekend! I can’t tell if I am slowly adapting, but this summer is more pleasant so far than last year.
  • Monday brought an interesting meet, where we spoke about community. One particularly striking takeaway was that you can just lean into community as a support (and route) for learning something new. This is something I have never done before, because I don’t like being bad at things in public, but I have decided that I want to try!
  • Another weekday night, however, I turned down an invitation to do exactly that. Instead I went to the gym, and for the first time since 2022 at the big Waitrose in Putney, I bumped into someone I knew at the supermarket.
  • This week had three superb lunches. When did I stop having lunch with people? It’s great. Let’s do more of that?
  • As a lark, I have built my own spaced-repetition tool to support my classwork. It’s somewhere in the middle of Anki and WaniKani, and I’m already finding it useful. In fact, I wish I had it this time last year. I'm toying with opening it up to other people.
  • Also: There is now a robot posting daily reading practice in my times channel. It’s deliberately stretchy, and again, I wish I had done this sooner.
  • That’s input and memorisation basically sorted: I need to find more opportunities to speak (and write) Japanese in a low-stakes way. Lightning didn't strike twice, and avoiding the booze has taken away my most plentiful opportunity in snack bars.
  • Thursday brought Tonkatsu, Friday brought Tonkotsu. Both were pretty good. Mocktail in Shibuya was powerful.
  • Kanda Bon Odori was a strange but good time. I spent 3 hours struggling to copy the right moves, as our concentric circles compressed into a mess of people. Something about mirror neuron activation.
  • Quietly, but surely.
